transcript:
Header: 2026-08-18 15:00 UTC - Duration 42m
Attendees: Alex Chan (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Sierra Payments), Priya Nair (Sierra Eng Manager), Liam O'Connor (Sierra Security)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm alex chan, i'm the account owner for sierra payments. maya from the se team with us too. how are you all?
[00:10] Carlos: good thanks, alex. busy week but excited to chat - we want to run through renewal options and expansion across regions.
[00:18] Priya: yeah we were hoping to lock down capacity for q4 and talk APAC.
[00:25] Alex: perfect. agenda - review current usage, discuss dedicated capacity upgrade, APAC region availability and timeline, contract term options, security questions, and next steps. sound good?
[00:34] Liam: yeah that's great. i have a few security items i want to cover near the end.
[00:37] Maya: i'll also cover what the dedicated offering looks like under the hood - batching, kv cache, and how we handle isolation. note: the transcript may sometimes say KV "cash" - ha - that's a transcribe quirk.
[00:48] Carlos: thanks, maya. first quick context: our current plan is hosted, average 150 qps across our payments pre-auth service, peak 320 qps during promos. latency target is p95 < 120ms token generation for short-forms. cost has been creeping and we'd like committed pricing if we can guarantee capacity.
[01:12] Alex: okay that's helpful. currently you're on our standard hosted tier with some autoscale, right?
[01:16] Carlos: yes, hosted with preferenced routing to us-east. we're seeing higher latency for APAC users and want options: dedicated in us-east + additional APAC regions, or a private deployment for PCI-adjacent workloads.
[01:31] Maya: technically, we can do a Dedicated pool in us-east and spin up dedicated pools in two APAC regions - tokyo and singapore - on a reserved commit. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolated GPU pools, plus SLA-backed latency. private / on-prem is possible but requires a pilot and longer lead time - typically 4-8 weeks for packaging and networking.
[01:54] Priya: lead time is key. for q4 rollout we need APAC by late october ideally. is that feasible?
[02:02] Maya: for standard dedicated in our cloud it's feasible - we can reserve capacity and confirm by end of august to hit late october; for private on-prem it might slip beyond that, depends on network approvals.
[02:12] Carlos: price-wise, what's committed pricing look like for an extra 6-8 A100-equivalent GPUs?
[02:18] Alex: i'll send specific numbers after this call. ballpark, committed monthly reserved capacity gives 20-30% discount vs on-demand. we also offer burst capacity for spiky traffic.
[02:28] Liam: on the security side, we need to confirm if keystores can be integrated with our existing KMS and if you support customer-managed keys/HSM. also SOC2 artifacts and audit logs retention periods are critical.
[02:42] Maya: yes we support KMS integrations and HSM for private deployments; for Hosted & Dedicated we have KMS integrations and can offer customer-managed key options for private. SOC2 reports and ISO artifacts can be shared under an NDA. audit logs are available; retention windows can be extended as an add-on.
[03:01] Priya: does dedicated separate customer data at rest or just by tenant? we need clear isolation for our payment tokens.
[03:08] Maya: Dedicated separates compute and storage per customer pool - there is tenant isolation at the compute and storage layers; for extra assurance we recommend private deployment or bring-your-own-key.
[03:18] Carlos: okay good. a few tradeoffs to discuss: dedicated + KMS vs private on-prem. dedicated hits our timeline but private is preferred for regulatory controls. maybe a hybrid: dedicated for the bulk and a private enclave for the most sensitive flows.
[03:33] Alex: that's a common pattern. we can design a routing policy so lower-sensitivity requests go to dedicated hosted endpoints and the sensitive tokens route to private. fallback policies are possible too.
[03:43] Priya: about performance - can you give us expected p95 latency numbers for the dedicated pool for our payloads? our sequences are short, mostly 16-64 tokens.
[03:52] Maya: for short sequences on A100 class with our continuous batching and prefix caching, p95 token generation is typically under 100-140ms depending on burstiness. we'll add sample numbers to the benchmark doc. note: model choice matters - quantized variants reduce cost but may affect quality.
[04:13] Carlos: model variants - are you recommending a quantized LLM or a full fp16 model for our use case?
[04:19] Maya: start with a quantized variant in dedicated to hit cost targets; we can run quality gating via eval prompt sets. if there are regressions, we can move to fp16 for specific routes.
[04:30] Liam: logging - we need request-level tracing for audits, and the ability to redact PII in logs.
[04:36] Maya: tracing hooks and per-route logs exist; redaction is configurable and we can show how to redact tokens at the SDK level.
[04:44] Carlos: ok same for role-based access? engineers vs ops vs security?
[04:49] Alex: yes RBAC with SSO/SAML integration is supported; we can map roles to routes and tokens.
[04:55] Priya: what's involved operationally to move from hosted to dedicated - is there a code change?
[05:00] Maya: minimal. same API surface, you can pin model versions and routes. you may update endpoint host or route mapping; SDK config change. we also provide migration guides and rollout tooling for canary flips and traffic splits.
[05:13] Carlos: great. question on SLAs - 99.9% uptime for dedicated?
[05:18] Alex: dedicated comes with an SLA; exact numbers and credits will be in the contract addendum.
[05:23] Priya: let's talk numbers for committed term. We're considering a 12-month extension with a commit to 8 GPUs and an option to scale to 16 if needed. What discounts and penalties for underuse?
[05:34] Alex: we offer step tiers: a base commit with guaranteed discount, and usage true-up each month. underuse credits can be negotiated in the contract; i'll put options in the pricing doc.
[05:43] Liam: does the committed pricing cover APAC region instances or is that separate?
[05:47] Maya: APAC region capacity is billed similarly but capacity provisioning differs by region. we can include APAC pools in the same commitment if we plan ahead; otherwise region add-ons apply.
[05:58] Carlos: timeline: we need APAC ready by late oct, commit decision by end of august. can you confirm region availability?
[06:07] Maya: yes i can check and confirm by monday - tokyo and singapore have availability but i'll confirm exact GPU types.
[06:14] Alex: noted - action: i'll follow up with pricing and contract options by monday 8/23.
[06:20] Priya: i'd like to see a sample PnL or cost-per-transaction model with the committed pricing vs on-demand.
[06:27] Alex: we'll include a cost model sheet with examples.
[06:30] Carlos: about the on-prem pilot - can we scope a 2-week benchmark window with sample traffic and acceptance criteria?
[06:36] Maya: yes we recommend a 2-week run with synthetic and replay traffic; acceptance criteria: p95 latency < 140ms and throughput to meet peak qps with <10% error rate. we'll provide a plan.
[06:49] Liam: for the pilot network, we'd need a checklist for firewall rules, VPC peering, and KMS endpoints. can you share that?
[06:57] Maya: i'll attach our private deployment network checklist to the benchmark plan.
[07:02] Alex: do you have any hard blockers on security that would stop you from pursuing dedicated?
[07:07] Liam: not blockers, more like gating items. KMS integration and audit docs are the big ones, plus confirmation of data residency for token logs.
[07:17] Alex: understood. we'll provide SOC2 report, ISO artifacts under NDA, and the KMS integration guide.
[07:24] Priya: one more question - what's the support model during the pilot and after?
[07:28] Alex: pilots get SE support and weekly check-ins; Dedicated customers get a support tier with faster SLAs, plus escalation paths. we'll include support tiers in the pricing doc.
[07:39] Carlos: ok great. anything else from the redwood side, maya?
[07:43] Maya: just to confirm the benchmark will include the models you want to test, the traffic profile, and the exact metrics we measure. sometimes the transcript says "quantize" as "can I size" when it shouldn't - ignore weird transcribe words.
[07:56] Priya: ha noted.
[08:00] (brief cross talk)
[08:18] Alex: recap - alex to send pricing & contract options including committed tiers and APAC pooling; maya to send benchmark plan and network checklist; liam to share compliance constraints; carlos to share traffic profile. follow-up meeting to schedule week of 2026-09-07 to kick off pilot.
[08:35] Carlos: yes that works, thanks everyone.
[08:38] Priya: thanks, looking forward.
[08:40] Liam: thanks all.
[08:42] Alex: thanks, we'll email the docs. end.

Notes: transcript has occasional speech-to-text errors (proper nouns, acronyms). references shared: pricing sheet (link: /redwood/pricing/CRM-78942), SOC2 pack (link: /redwood/security/soc2-2026), benchmark template (link: /redwood/benchmarks/pilot-template).
